title: chore(governance): the guard scripts join the governed register, `.claude/**` lands by declared rule-change, a declared narrowing waits for the maintainer
body:

_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu72Wnwx2ESew3k8vGRt7jiX)_

Fixes #35321

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Rule-change: yes

Branch note for the Duplicate Fix Guard: `claude/project-thread-ndkip6` is the branch the card thread's harness assigns, and the claim comment on the card names it; it carries no issue number by construction.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感。车队内部：改动「判定谁能合并」的那几件工具本身、改动车队规则条文，今后都要等你亲手批准；只改措辞和流程的车队文档仍由席位凭复核落地，但提交时必须声明「没有改规则」，复核记录也要确认这一点；会让现有应用报错的规范收紧，入队前同样要等你批准。
- 为什么做：属于「评审分工」这一轮整理，把你今天上午确认的几点落成机器检查——今天改守门工具本身可以绕开所有拦截。
- 出错会怎样：声明或复核记录缺失时，相关改动会被合并队列拦下等你批，不会误放行；本 PR 合并后有七个在途改动会先被拦下（明细见下文英文部分），补上声明或由你批准即可放行；拦错了你批准一次即可放行，整个改动可以一次撤回。
- 要你做什么：审阅并批准本 PR（它自己就改了规则条文和守门工具）。

## Source

The card's source line, the maintainer (Warren), 2026-11-19, review-split discussion thread, verbatim and untranslated:

> 03:16Z 「以上都同意」
> 03:17Z 「北极星、AGENTS.md、改车队规则的技能条文（谁能做什么、怎么定级、怎么合并）也需要fable 吧」
> 03:17Z 「spec：收紧作者能写的东西（会让现有应用报错），也需要fable 吧？」
> 04:24Z 「1+2+4」
> 04:30Z 「「已裁定的照抄只核对、不再审」 同意」

Point 1 of 「1+2+4」 returns fleet rule text to the maintainer and overrides the 2026-09-18 ruling where that ruling handed all of `.claude/**` to the seats on a contract review. Rule text is: what an agent may do without him (merge, bypass checks, change repository settings); what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope); what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions). Process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves stay with the reviewer.

## What changes

The card's five items, in its order, then the authors' side added in the patch round.

1. **The guard instruments are register rows, Tier H, scoped to objectstack.** Four exact rows join `GOVERNED_SURFACES`: `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`. The card's conditional was measured before the edit: `readWorkflowDiff` could read an edit to the guard's own workflow file as Tier S, so `.github/workflows/governed-surface-guard.yml` joins `WORKFLOW_TIER_H_FILES` (seven always-H workflow files now). `.github/CODEOWNERS` mirrors the four rows, which `codeownersMirrorVerdict` demands.
2. **`.claude/**` splits by declaration.** The row keeps `tier: S` and gains `ruleChange`; `applyRuleChangeSplit` runs last in the tier chain and answers Tier H unless the PR body carries one bare line-start declaration of `none` (or of `ruled` together with one bare line-start ruling reference) and the PASS record on the current head carries `Rule-change-verified:` with the same value. A missing line, a `yes`, a quoted, fenced or doubled line, or a record that does not verify is Tier H. `.claude/settings*.json` and everything under `.claude/hooks/` are Tier H by path whatever is declared, and CODEOWNERS now carries a line for each. `ui/.claude/**` and every other repository's `.claude/**` stay Tier H.
   - Path-only callers of `governedTierFor` and `testVerdict` (`--test`, `--branch`) now answer Tier H for `.claude/**`: a path list cannot say what a body declares.
   - At the queue the body is read on the pull read the head already costs. The declaration alone gives Tier S there, and the record leg then requires stands, PASS and the verified line (`ruleChangeRecordVerdict`); a record carried across a head move must not have crossed a `.claude/**` hunk.
   - `--pr` stages the record read the way the low-risk arm does (pending, read, asked again).
3. **A declared narrowing lands like Tier H.** A new leg of the queue guard, `merge_group` only, reads every queued pull's body and every changeset its commit carries, line by line with the fleet's two readers. A declared narrowing (the narrowed value of the metadata-protocol line, or the narrowing arm on either value of the clause line) is refused on exit 10 until both halves are on record: an authorized APPROVED review, and a PASS contract review that stands on the current head. `added`, `semantic`, `none` and a bare clause line cost one already-memoized pull read and change nothing. Unreadable inputs refuse on exit 11. Exit precedence is governed, then size, then narrowed.
   - Measuring the PR template for item 6 found a defect in this leg as first pushed: the template's unfilled menu line (the metadata-protocol key followed by its four kinds joined by bars) was read as a declared narrowing, and the changeset check passes such a body when the line is moot, so a pull that left the template untouched would have been refused at the queue. Now exactly that menu, as the template spells it, declares nothing (`UNFILLED_PROTOCOL_MENU`, built from the reader's own kind list); a partial menu that still spells the narrowed kind counts as before. The pin reads the template file from disk.
4. **The `workflows` row adds `hotcrm`**, as the audit mirror: a merged hotcrm workflow change now produces a row in the sweep. `objectos` and `mobile` stay out.
5. **Prose.** `AGENTS.md` Prime Directive #14 names the four instruments and states the split in one sentence; the pm-dispatch path-fork region names the same surfaces, the split and the declared-narrowing landing; `references/contract-review.md` names the record's `Rule-change-verified:` line, and `record-recognisers.mjs --template` and `--brief-template` print it (shipped as `yes`, so an unedited paste lands nothing) with one duty wording both share.
6. **Authors are told to write the declaration.** Two files, added on the file surface the claim was widened to:
   - The developer agent's instruction file (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`), in its definition of done: a diff that touches the root `.claude/**` tree owes the PR body one line-start declaration, judged from the diff. It gives the three values (`none`: no fleet rule changed, with the three kinds of rule named; `yes`: one changed; `ruled`: the text copies a ruling already made), says `ruled` owes a second line-start line quoting the maintainer with source and time and says a missing line lands as Tier H like `yes`.
   - The claim template in the pm-dispatch skill file carries no clause for it. One was added in the first patch round and taken back out at head `9a1758ee`, when `main` began to count the skill files in bytes with no headroom (the deletions are listed under Acceptance notes). The developer is taught by the agent file, and the seat by the Tier S line of the path-fork region.
   - `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: an italic note under the two declaration lines, asking for the line only when the pull changes a file under `.claude/`. The template carries no fillable line for it, so an unfilled template still reads as `missing`, as it did before. Measured before choosing the wording: no script or workflow reads the template file, the two existing line readers answer the same on the new template as on the old one, and the key is read only by the register's tier reading and only for a pull that hits the `.claude/**` row. No guard starts requiring the line on other pulls.

Line budget: 1,751 changed lines (+1,602 / -149) over 9 files, against the 3,000-line human-merge line.

## Landing impact

From the merge of this PR on, every open pull whose diff touches the root `.claude/**` tree lands as Tier H until its body carries the line-start declaration and the PASS record on its current head carries the verified line. `.claude/settings*.json` and `.claude/hooks/**` are Tier H whatever is declared.

Read again at head `9a1758ee`, over all 52 open pulls (this one included), each pull's full file list:

- #35443 (ready for review; `.claude/settings.json` only). Tier S today. Tier H by path after the merge, whatever it declares. Its body carries no declaration line.

No other open pull touches the root `.claude/**` tree, the four instrument files, the guard's workflow file or `ui/.claude/**`.

Item 3 changes a second set of open pulls, whatever paths they touch: from the merge on, a pull whose body or changeset declares a narrowing is refused at the queue until an authorized approval (or the authorized account's own enqueue) and a standing PASS contract review are on its head. Read at the same pass, by running this head's own reader, `narrowingDeclarationsIn`, over every open pull body:

- #35604, #34738, #34223, #35664, #35697 and #35718 (all drafts): each body carries a clause line with the narrowing arm.

Only pull bodies were read for this list. A narrowing declared in a changeset alone is read by the leg at the queue and is not listed here.

The seat sends a notice to the owning seats of the pulls named in this section before this PR lands. The notices are sent: PR comment 7019977853 records those for #35443, #35604, #34738 and #34223, and the seat's notices for #35664, #35697 and #35718 are comments 7030716558, 7030722099 and 7030728219.

## Tests

Head `9a1758ee`, which has `main` at `a457b515` merged in. Every exit code below was captured before any pipe.

- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 959 assertions. New battery of 40 cases pins item 1 and item 2: each guard file is H in objectstack and ungoverned elsewhere; a `.claude/` wording path with both lines is S; a missing line, `yes`, an unverified record, a quoted, fenced or doubled line are H; settings and hooks are H by path with both lines on record; hotcrm workflows are governed.
- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 637 cases. Two new batteries (26 and 24 cases): the same branches driven end to end at the queue, the CODEOWNERS mirror, and the narrowed leg (declared without approval is refused on 10; `added` is unchanged on one pull read; both halves clear; each half alone refuses and names the missing half; unreadable inputs refuse on 11; the PR template left unfilled declares no narrowing, a partial menu still does; the narrowed kind on a runtime-only path, in five body shapes, is refused on a default-tier record and cleared on an at-tier one).
- `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 456 cases. The template the tool prints is driven through the queue guard: with the reviewer's own `none` it clears, pasted unedited it does not.
- `pnpm check:pm-governed-prose`: exit 0, both regions name all 17 rows that govern objectstack. `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet`: exit 0, counted in bytes since `main` at `a457b515`, with `AGENTS.md` at 78,011 of 78,106, the skill file at 33,872 of 33,872, the developer agent file at 38,846 of 38,848 and the review reference at 6,416 of 6,419. This PR edits no ceiling row. `pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint`: exit 0.

<details>
<summary>One-time ablations (not kept as tests): three mutations, each red, each restored</summary>

A1 to A3 ran at the earlier head `cd8dab31`; the patch round changed one tested behaviour (the unfilled-menu exemption), ablated at `eb947a21` as A4; the second patch round changed one more (the record half holds the narrowing face), ablated at `eb455747` as A5. Head `9a1758ee` changes prose only and no tested behaviour. All ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode on committed code; after each, the tool printed the restored blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Expected direction was red in every leg but one, noted below.

- A1, a `yes` declaration no longer refused (one line in `ruleChangeVerdict`): register self-test exit 1 with 4 failures; queue-guard self-test exit 1, failing `Rule-change-yes-is-Tier-H-refused-whatever-the-record-says`.
- A2, the `guard-queue` row's exact path changed: register self-test exit 1 with 2 failures; queue-guard self-test exit 1 on four CODEOWNERS mirror pins. The prose gate stayed green on this mutation: it reads the row's `glob`, which the mutation left alone, so that leg measured nothing about the prose gate.
- A3, the human half of the narrowed leg no longer required: queue-guard self-test exit 1, failing `narrowed-declaration-without-approval-is-REFUSED-on-its-own-code` and three sibling pins.
- A4, at `eb947a21`, the unfilled-menu exemption removed from `narrowingDeclarationsIn`: queue-guard self-test exit 1, 1 of 636 cases failed, the pin `the-pull-request-template-left-UNFILLED-declares-no-narrowing-and-a-partial-menu-still-does`. A first attempt with an empty replacement was refused by the tool before the command ran and measured nothing; the run quoted is the second.
- A5, at `eb455747`, the hold removed from `recordVerdict`: queue-guard self-test exit 1, 1 of 637 cases failed, the pin `the-narrowed-kind-on-a-runtime-only-path-holds-the-narrowing-faces-tier-a-default-tier-record-is-REFUSED-an-at-tier-one-CLEARS`, with the default-tier record clearing and the at-tier record refused in three of its shapes, which is what the same pin read on the code before the change.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

Deliberate choices a reviewer should see, and what is left outside this PR.

- The record half of the narrowed leg holds the narrowing face's tier whichever line carries the declaration (the clause line's arm or the metadata-protocol line's narrowed kind), so a default-tier record does not clear it and an at-tier record does; a schema or governed path still decides first.
- **The human half of the narrowed leg also counts the maintainer's own enqueue.** The card says an authorized APPROVED review; the 2026-10-26 ruling made an enqueue from an authorized account the same act for every landing the guard judges, so the leg accepts either and still requires the PASS record. Dropping the enqueue arm is a one-line change if the approver wants the approval alone; the question was put to the coordinator, who left it here for the approver.
- **Two readers do not chain the split and still read the raw row's Tier S**: the relay's review-request plan and the patrol's landing row, both outside this card's file surface. Neither decides a landing; the queue guard does. Effect: a pull that declares a rule change is refused at the queue but is not auto-routed to the maintainer by the relay. CODEOWNERS routes the settings and hooks paths. A follow-up card for the two readers is filed by the card thread, not in this PR.
- **The PR template gets a note, not a fillable line.** A fillable line would sit in every pull's body and be read as a declaration on pulls it does not concern; the note keeps the unfilled reading at `missing`.
- **The early-warning (`pull_request`) leg reads no body**, so it names a `.claude/**` diff as Tier H until the body is read, and never reddens.
- **The post-merge sweep has no audit leg for the split**; it lists the merge with its approver and merger as before.
- **hotcrm's own half** (its instruction file listing workflows as governed) is a separate PR in that repository.
- **Not on the register**: the readers the guard imports (the clause-line readers, the patrol module, the relay op table, the tier data file) and the `ui/` copy of the queue guard, which belongs to its own card.
- **A near-arm spelling counts as a declared narrowing** (fail closed); a narrowing nobody declared stays the contract review's finding.
- **The narrowed rule's prose home is one clause in the path-fork region**; Prime Directive #14 is about governed paths and was left to items 1 and 2.
- **The refusal string of the narrowed leg cites its ruling by date**; the quotation lives in the script header.
- **Content deleted to stay at the ceilings** (no ceiling moved; the first two rounds paid in lines, and head `9a1758ee` pays in bytes). `AGENTS.md` #14: the parenthetical after `.claude/**`, the sentence describing when the prose gate reds (shortened), the comment id after `pr_dequeue`, the rationale clause after the no-approving-review rule, the sentence about CODEOWNERS and the relay routing, the restated "tiered by the register" clause, and one repeated "on a PR whose diff touches a governed surface". Path-fork region: the restated "split before acting" clause, the bullet restating the developer agent's own rule for the reader summary, and the "(该面独占)" restatement. Review reference: the words saying who reads the security line, which the template legend carries. Developer agent file (three lines added, three paid, at the earlier heads): the bullet restating that one foreground blocking wait is the only wait shape, and the bullet restating that no lock, sibling build or watcher wakes the agent, both already said by the resource rules above them; two pointer lines to the body-sanitizer rule in `AGENTS.md` merged into one. At head `9a1758ee`, after the merge of `main` left the skill file 377 bytes and the developer agent file 38 bytes over their new byte ceilings: the claim-template clause added in the first patch round is taken back out; in the path-fork region the three lines that list the governed surfaces become one list line, with the `GOVERNED_REPOS` sentence on a line of its own, the two guard lines become one, and the tag 「(本仓)」 and one word of the skills-lane exception are dropped; in the developer agent file the three declaration lines become two, and the note that no other line may lead with the key is dropped (a second such line reads as Tier H at the guard, which prints the reason).
- **Local narrowing of verification**: `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` answered exit 3, prerequisite not met (it needs the CLI and example builds); NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI. The diff touches no package, so there is no build closure and no package test owed.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`: the `ruleChangeVerdict` function and the register rows. Risk hunk: the order of its four checks, since Tier S is returned only with zero reasons.
2. `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: `ruleChangeRecordVerdict`, `narrowedReading` and `narrowingDeclarationsIn`. Risk hunks: the queue leg defers the record to its own record leg, so the verified line is enforced there and nowhere earlier; the unfilled-menu exemption must stay an exact match.
3. `AGENTS.md` Prime Directive #14 and the two added lines in `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`: the new sentences, and the deletions listed above.

Two-minute check: run `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`. Expected: exit 3, `landing tier: H`, the row named `the dispatch gates and the contract-review tier they declare`. On `main` the same command answers 0 hits.

<details>
<summary>Derived gate union</summary>

At head `eb455747`: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 78 commands from the 9 changed paths, one more than at the head before it (`pnpm check:agent-model-declared`, which reads the agent files). All 78 ran at that head, exit code recorded per command: 77 exit 0, 1 exit 3 (`pnpm check:i18n-coverage`, prerequisite not met). Nothing was carried from an earlier head. `--ran` reconciliation: `78 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 77 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`. `pnpm check:nul-bytes` and `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` are among the 77. The derivation printed a stale-tree note (12 commits behind `origin/main`, one derivation input changed there); the branch was not merged with `origin/main` at that head.

At head `9a1758ee`: `main` at `a457b515` is merged in (no conflict), and one commit edits two files, the pm-dispatch skill file and the developer agent file. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --paths` over those two files derived 26 commands; all 26 ran at this head and exited 0, the three self-tests and the prose, ratchet and id-lint gates quoted under Tests among them. The other 52 commands are carried from `eb455747` and left to CI on this head. `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` at this head: clean against `origin/main` and the one open pull that shares a file (#35582, `AGENTS.md`).

</details>
